creem.activation_decision_2026-09-05: NOT activating now, despite approval. Creem's role is Merchant-of-Record payment/checkout infrastructure -- the same job Stripe already does live for this experiment (prod_V8TDzCnDU7y2r9, $19, Managed Payments + automatic tax). Approval removes the 'is it usable' uncertainty but does not create a Net-Profit case on its own: no buyer would newly discover the product through Creem (it has no marketplace/search surface, unlike Etsy or Gumroad), so building it would only offer existing buyers a second checkout for the same product -- pure substitution, not incremental reach. Building it now would cost real AI-compute (product config, checkout integration, workflow, docs, cost-ledger wiring) for zero expected incremental revenue, while Etsy (validated buyer search-intent, going live this same iteration) and watching Gumroad/Etsy for a first sale are both higher-expected-value uses of the same budget. Would reconsider only if a specific advantage over Stripe surfaces (e.g. materially lower fees, a market/currency Stripe can't serve, or a partner/embed distribution channel unique to Creem) -- none identified as of this decision.
creem.assessment: Even with account + API + approval all confirmed, Creem's role is Merchant-of-Record payment/billing infrastructure -- functionally the same job Stripe already does live, not a marketplace with its own buyer-search discovery. No distribution-value differentiator over Stripe has been identified. Deprioritized: approved and usable, but NOT being activated absent a specific identified advantage (would be redundant payment infra).

latest_result: The first deliberate distribution test failed at the reach stage, decisively: 0 impressions in ~33h. This answers the traffic-vs-offer question the test was built for -- it is reach, not offer. The reply-to-root X structure is a transparent LOG mechanism, not a distribution one; it cannot put the store in front of the owned audience. After 10 official days the three sales channels remain discovery-less, and the one owned qualified-traffic lever (the @KinoshitaTsks audience) has never actually been reached, because the only posting mechanism used (a threaded reply) has ~0 organic reach.

latest_strategy_decision: Reclassified the binding constraint from an offer/audience/traffic 'mismatch' (Day 9 hypothesis) to distribution REACH specifically, now that the test gives a clean top-of-funnel zero. The next distribution experiment must use a reach-capable mechanism. The leading candidate is a TOP-LEVEL post from the owned @KinoshitaTsks account (the only owned qualified-traffic lever), which would actually appear in followers' timelines -- unlike the threaded reply. Deliberately did NOT unilaterally build+fire top-level posting this run: it is a new outward use of the owner's personal public account beyond the reply-to-root commentary the owner reviewed/approved, so it is surfaced as a one-time account-owner-consent item (LOOP_PROTOCOL section 2 carve-out) rather than executed. The reply-commentary pipeline stays as-is (it is the experiment log). Held cadence 1x/day; the Day-11 fire executes the reach mechanism if consent lands. Did not edit the store (no one has seen it; editing would be evidence-free speculation).
latest_strategy_decision_ja: ボトルネックを、Day 9仮説の『オファー/オーディエンス/集客のミスマッチ』から具体的に『到達（リーチ）』へ再分類した——テストがファネル最上流のクリーンなゼロを示したため。次の集客実験は到達力のある仕組みを使う必要がある。有力候補は所有する@KinoshitaTsksアカウントからのトップレベル投稿（唯一の所有する質の高い集客レバー）で、スレッド内リプライと違いフォロワーのタイムラインに実際に表示される。今回、トップレベル投稿の実装・実行を独断では行わなかった：オーナーが確認・承認したルート投稿へのリプライ型コメンタリーを超える、オーナー個人の公開アカウントの新しい対外利用にあたるため、実行ではなく一度限りのアカウント所有者同意事項（LOOP_PROTOCOL第2節の例外）として提示する。リプライ型コメンタリーのパイプラインは現状維持（実験の記録用）。ケイデンスは1回/日を維持し、同意が得られればDay-11の実行で到達の仕組みを実行する。ストアは編集しない（誰も見ていない以上、編集は証拠のない推測になる）。
